Self-service, standalone download sets you can download and run.

::: {.callout-important}
Tools here ingest or produce assessment data — a map of where a tenant is weak.
Treat that data as **Controlled**: keep it in-boundary, share only with
authorized personnel, and do not publish raw findings. Remediation guidance is
**advisory** — apply changes only through your normal change-control process.
:::

## Federal Organization Compliance Series {#federal-organization-compliance-series}

An **eleven-volume, 60-book** program covering the network, identity, data-platform,
security-operations, governance, training, ServiceNow-automation, multi-cloud DDI,
day-2, and optional substrate-integration architecture required for **FedRAMP Moderate** authorization under FedRAMP 20x
rules (mandatory January 1, 2027).

**[Read the series →](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_0_Book_00a_OrgComp_Executive_Brief.qmd)**
— start with the two-page executive brief. Every book is browsable on this site and
carries a Word download button.

**Two editions, one source.** What you see here is the **federal edition**: written for
any federal agency, with no agency named. An **agency edition** renders from the same

All are **rebuilt from source on every deploy** — the `.docx` and `.md` are the
published **federal** renders (no agency identity, no internal marking), so no
fixed SHA-256 is published. The kit contains the federal edition only; the
agency edition is not distributed here.

::: {.callout-note}
**Hosted as release assets, not on this site.** These zips, `orgcomp-series-bundle.docx`,
and every per-book / per-section `*-bundle.docx` sitewide are large enough that
bundling them into the published site pushed the site's own build past GitHub
Pages' size guidance, so they all ship instead as assets on the rolling
[`downloads-latest` release](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/tag/downloads-latest) —
same "rebuilt from source on every deploy" semantics, just not part of the
site build itself. Every book and section page's own "download this as Word"
button is unaffected — only the *concatenated multi-page bundles* moved.
:::

## OrgPath Governance Series {#orgpath-governance-series}

**The governance expression of the UIAO substrate** — canon as the source of
truth, addressing as the governed namespace. OrgTree (organizational
hierarchy), OrgPath (the attribute path), and LocPath (location addressing)
give every identity, device, and policy a governed address.

**[Read the series →](../orgpath/index.qmd)** — the OrgPath hub is the front
door. Every page is browsable on this site and carries its own Word download
button.

| Download | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`orgpath-governance-series-latest.zip`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/download/downloads-latest/orgpath-governance-series-latest.zip) | The whole family as Word documents, in six folders — `Narrative/` (the OrgPath reading sequence, one `.docx` per book with its chapters concatenated), `Reference_Architecture/` (OrgTree, LocPath, the codebook, drift, delegation, dynamic groups, portability), `Implementation/` (the seven-step Intune + Azure Arc rollout), `Multi_Cloud/` (OrgPath beyond Microsoft), `Governance_Operations/` (the Active Governance Directory, federal AI identity governance, and the Help Desk / Cloud Services authority model), and `Whitepapers/` (the six governance-track papers — governance foundations, and positioning and vendor reads). Open **`INDEX.md`** first |

## OrgMod Modernization Series {#orgmod-modernization-series}

**The modernization expression of the UIAO substrate** — moving a legacy
estate forward *without rip-and-replace*, governed by the same spine. Active
Directory → Entra ID is the leading worked path, not the only one.

**[Read the series →](../orgmod/index.qmd)** — the OrgMod hub is the front
door.

| Download | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`orgmod-modernization-series-latest.zip`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/download/downloads-latest/orgmod-modernization-series-latest.zip) | The whole family as Word documents, in six folders — `Transformation_Narrative/` (Microsoft Client-Server to Hybrid-Cloud, chapter by chapter), `Guides/` (the modernization guide shelf: platform substrate, transformation engine, identity/OrgTree, directory migration, target surface, access plane, network transformation, program management), `Modernization_Specs/` (cloud, identity, SASE, SD-WAN, telemetry, zero trust), `Directory_Migration_Bridge/` (what replaces AD's implicit roles, and the adapter interfaces), `Whitepapers/` (the fourteen modernization-track papers — the AD → Entra ID arc, and network and infrastructure modernization), and `SQL_Server_Transformation/` (the worked consumer — narrative plus its executable companion). Open **`INDEX.md`** first |

Both kits are **rebuilt from source on every deploy** — the `.docx` are the
published site's own renders — so no fixed SHA-256 is published, and both ship
as assets on the same rolling
[`downloads-latest` release](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/tag/downloads-latest)
as everything above.

::: {.callout-note}
**How the shared `operational-guides/` tree is split.** That tree is OrgMod's
operational home, but four of its sub-sections are OrgPath's content and ship
in the **OrgPath** kit instead — the seven-step OrgPath implementation guides
(kit folder `Implementation/`), and the three steady-state governance
sub-sections in `Governance_Operations/`: the Active Governance Directory, the
federal AI identity governance kit, and the Help Desk / Cloud Services authority
model. The dividing question is whether a page's deliverable exists because an
estate is *moving* (OrgMod) or because an estate is *governed in steady state*
(OrgPath); a modernization runbook that happens to bind OrgPath — the Intune +
Azure Arc governed path, say — is still OrgMod. Every page in the tree reaches
exactly one of the two kits. The two `reference-architecture` pages that *are*
the AD infrastructure bridge (`directory-migration`, `adapters`) are the one
deliberate exception: they appear in both kits, because both hubs name them.

**Whitepapers are selected, not swept.** The whitepaper section serves all four
pillars, so neither kit takes it wholesale. Both selections follow the
section's own
[reading guide](../customer-documents/whitepapers/reading-guide.qmd), which
already groups the papers into six tracks by the question they answer: the
**OrgMod** kit takes Track 2 (Identity & Directory Modernization) and Track 4
(Network & Infrastructure Modernization) plus the Track 1 paper that guide
names as the bridge into Track 2 — fourteen papers; the **OrgPath** kit takes
the rest of Track 1 (Governance Foundations) and Track 6 (Positioning,
Comparison & Vendor Reads) — six. The two papers the guide cross-lists across a
modernization and a governance track are single-homed in their primary track's
kit, so the two selections are disjoint. Tracks 3 and 5 are compliance
material and reach neither kit. The
[whitepapers section](../customer-documents/whitepapers/index.qmd) publishes
its own complete zip regardless.
:::

## ScubaDrift

**Drift, exception-lifecycle, and continuous-monitoring gating on top of CISA
ScubaGear.** ScubaGear assesses a Microsoft 365 tenant against the CISA SCuBA
baselines; ScubaDrift adds the operational layer it leaves out — run-to-run
drift, risk-acceptance lifecycle, a continuous-monitoring gate, and remediation
**SLA aging** mapped to CISA BOD 25-01, NIST SP 800-137 (ISCM), NIST 800-53
CA-7, and FedRAMP ConMon. It stands on the sanctioned tool and never touches a
tenant — it reads ScubaGear's JSON output. Python 3.10+, zero runtime
dependencies.

| Download | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`scubadrift-latest.zip`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/download/downloads-latest/scubadrift-latest.zip) | Runnable package — source, 47-test suite, examples, figure sources, and `ScubaDrift-Documentation.docx` |
| [`ScubaDrift-Documentation.docx`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/releases/download/downloads-latest/ScubaDrift-Documentation.docx) | The full documentation as a single Word document (also inside the zip) |

Quick start:

```bash
unzip scubadrift-latest.zip && cd scubadrift
pip install .            # or: pip install '.[yaml]'
scubadrift gate --results ScubaResults.json --exceptions exceptions.yaml
```

Both artifacts are **rebuilt on every deploy** from source (`tools/scubadrift/`),
so no fixed SHA-256 is published here. A versioned archive
(`scubadrift-<version>.zip`) is published alongside the `-latest` alias.

## Verifying a download

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\download.zip -Algorithm SHA256
# compare the output to the SHA-256 listed above before running
# then run the bundled test suite (where applicable):
#   pip install '.[dev]' ; pytest -q
```
